thread:
maria: Quick follow-up from the graded-quant RFC — we need to nail the ops handshake and lifecycle for the FP8 -> INT8 -> 4-bit paths. A few open questions below, please chime in.

dan: Ack. can you list the specific handoff points you mean?

maria: Sure — three hotspots: 1) when runtime signals degraded accuracy and should request a fallback, 2) how ops enforce customer overrides (e.g., customer pins to int8), 3) warmup / cache priming when switching quant lanes.

priya: For (1) I think we should rely on a single small signal from runtime: degscore (0..1). If degscore < 0.85 for N=3 samples -> suggest fallback. Ops can decide to accept or suppress.

tom: Degscore is fine but we need to avoid noisy oscillation. Suggest hysteresis + min-duration. e.g. require 3 consecutive windows OR 10s cooldown after a switch.

maria: Agreed. Example config sketch I used in the RFC:
```
quant_handshake:
  preferred: ["fp8","int8","4bit"]
  fallback_rules:
    - condition: "degscore < 0.85 and samples>=3"
      action: request_fallback
    - condition: "latency > 150ms"
      action: prefer_lower_precision
  cooldown_s: 10
  min_run_s: 30
```

ezra: Two quick ops concerns: 1) telemetry cardinality if degscore is per-token, 2) customer overrides need audit trail. We should emit an event: quant.change.requested / quant.change.applied with reason+trace_id.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary rollout 3 -> 3 started for channel eng-ml at 6581239999.

jen: On the customer override model, we must allow: pin_to = [fp8,int8,4bit] OR pin_level = "max_quality". Also a way to specify "allow_degradation: false".

priya: Implementation detail: runtime will attach a short vector in response headers: X-Quant-Info: lane=fp8;deg=0.78;reason=prompt_len
That keeps the handshake small and language-agnostic.

dan: Ops acceptance criteria request: 1) no additional >1% latency p95 when the handshake is enabled, 2) rollback ability via console toggle, 3) canary on 5% traffic with automatic revert on error spike.

maria: I'll draft a short ops playbook with those criteria. Question: do we want a soft-fallback (simulate fallback but still serve original for a %) for rollout comparisons?

tom: Yes — shadow fallback is invaluable for QA. We can run the fallback in shadow mode and collect degscore/quality delta without impacting customers. Shadow mode needs to be opt-in per-customer to respect compute billing.

ezra: Also add a small A/B harness to compare sampling-based metrics (ROUGE/EMB-sim) on a rolling prompt set. We should store a 1k prompt seed bank for each major endpoint.

jen: Action items I volunteer for: 1) playbook draft, 2) console toggle prototype, 3) audit-event schema. ETA: EOW if nobody objects.

maria: Thanks! final Q: what about small-batch performance artifacts when switching lanes mid-request (longctx)? Do we reject switching mid-response?

priya: For now: disallow lane switch mid-stream; runtime should only switch between requests. We'll mark longctx switch behavior as future work.

dan: Sounds safe. If we hit cases where switching mid-stream is necessary, we'll need a migration plan for KV cache adaptation.

maria: Great — if no objections I'll post a short RFC addendum with the config sketch and action items. :thumbsup:

jen: No objections from me. +1.

ezra: +1. small note: add logging for "why" fallback chosen (deg vs latency vs manual).

ops-bot: [incident-bot] Reminder: if fallback causes customer error-rate > 1%, revert auto-canary.

maria: OK closing for now; will ping when addendum + PR are up. Thanks everyone.
